source: វិធានការចម្រុះគ្រប់គ្រងដំណាំ លើដំណាំស្រូវ (Integrated Pest Management on Rice), training slide deck, Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries of Battambang province, presented by Ms. Yem Sophy, Oct 20, 2017 (contact: ysophy168@gmail.com, 012 558 312)
text: Rice leaffolder (Cnaphalocrocis medinalis) moths are yellowish-brown; larvae fold and glue a rice leaf into a tube using silk thread and feed by scraping the green leaf tissue from inside the fold, leaving a pale, papery, scraped patch visible from outside. Moths are most active at dusk; the egg stage lasts about 1-2 days before hatching, and a single female can lay up to roughly 300 eggs over her lifetime of about 10 days. Damage guidance: leaf damage of up to about 50% of leaf area before heading generally does not reduce yield meaningfully since the plant compensates, but damage to the flag leaf around heading time can cut yield by about 50% or more because that leaf feeds grain fill directly. Natural enemies noted include spiders and small parasitic/predatory beetles found in the same field.
